Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No evidence of job seeker registry or labour market information system integration with national data exchange platform.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original citation (UNCDF Inclusive Digital Economy Scorecard 2021) is a general digital-economy assessment and does not specifically address employment services integration; it did not support the original score. Fresh evidence shows Burkina Faso's national employment agency (ANPE) has operated a digital job-seeker registration and recruitment platform (anpebf.com) since 2021, a digital work-card e-service (cartedetravail.anpe.gov.bf), and has been developing a further online recruitment/registration platform since September 2024, alongside the youth-focused YouthConnekt Burkina portal. No evidence was found that these sector-specific systems are integrated with the national government data exchange, or with each other. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated), since a standalone system is now confirmed to exist without cross-government integration.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso's national employment agency (ANPE) operates a digital job-seeker registration and recruitment platform (anpebf.com, live since 2021) and a digital work-card e-service, with a further online recruitment portal under development since September 2024. The youth employment portal YouthConnekt Burkina also provides job-related information. These systems function independently, with no evidence of integration with the national government data exchange platform or with unemployment insurance or broader labour market information systems.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No specific evidence of court records or case management integration with national data exchange systems. Security sector digital expenditure noted as non-transparent (IMF). Digital governance reforms focus on public finance and administration, not specifically justice systems.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original IMF source could not be retrieved (repeated crawl timeout on elibrary.imf.org) and, per the original comment, addressed security-sector budget opacity rather than justice-system data integration directly, so it did not support the score. Fresh evidence shows Burkina Faso has launched a nationwide e-casier judiciaire (criminal record) platform and, on 15 December 2025, three further justice e-services: justice-penale.gov.bf (online criminal complaints and case tracking), e-permis-communiquer.gov.bf (prison visit permits) and e-actes-rccm.gov.bf (business registry acts). These sit within a World Bank-financed 'dematerialisation of the penal and administrative judicial chain' project (PACT DIGITAL, 2025-2027), confirmed operational by the World Bank's Implementation Status Report (archived 28 December 2025). Interconnection between justice-sector systems and other government platforms was still being assessed as of June 2025, so full data-exchange integration is not yet evidenced. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development).
revised_comments: Burkina Faso has launched a nationwide electronic criminal-record platform (e-casier judiciaire) and, from December 2025, an online criminal-complaint and case-tracking platform (justice-penale.gov.bf), a prison-visit permit e-service (e-permis-communiquer.gov.bf) and an online business-registry service (e-actes-rccm.gov.bf). These form part of a World Bank-financed programme to digitise the penal and administrative judicial chain, run jointly by the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Digital Transition between 2025 and 2027. Interconnection of these systems with each other and with the wider government data exchange remains under active development.

Comments: Quarterly budget execution reports published online (IMF 2024 condition). Limited overall transparency on data exchange operations.

revision_notes: The IMF source could not be re-verified (crawl timeout on elibrary.imf.org on two attempts); the LinkedIn post is also not independently verifiable as its content is not accessible without a logged-in session. Fresh evidence found: the World Bank's Implementation Status and Results Report for the Burkina Faso Digital Acceleration Project (PACTDIGITAL) is a periodic, publicly disclosed document (the fourth in the series, archived 28 December 2025) covering progress on digital-government platforms, plus an operational citizen grievance mechanism and annual consultations. Burkina Faso also holds an Open Government Partnership commitment (BF0011) to publish ministry data in open formats. This constitutes recurring public reporting going beyond 'limited disclosure', though still short of a dedicated public dashboard specifically for data exchange operations. Recalculated from 2 (Low) to 3 (Moderate = Annual Reports); value name label also brought into line with the metadata scale.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso's digital transformation programme (PACTDIGITAL), which underpins much of the government's data-exchange infrastructure, is subject to periodic public reporting through the World Bank's Implementation Status and Results Reports, the latest published in December 2025, alongside an operational citizen grievance mechanism and annual public consultations. The country also holds an Open Government Partnership commitment to publish ministry data in open formats. There is, however, no consolidated public dashboard or dedicated annual report specifically on data exchange governance and data-sharing agreements.
